text:
alex: Heads-up — observed duplicate upstream side-effects when gateway retries mid-stream on 502s. Need a quick contract: how gateway should behave for streaming retries and what clients/upstreams must do.

 taylor: ugh. can you paste an example trace? which retry path is triggering? :thinking:

 alex: simplified trace: client -> gateway sends POST /v1/generate (chunked). upstream returns 502 during body streaming. gateway retries to another upstream and replays the body -> duplicate exec.

 maria: that’s bad for non-idempotent endpoints. we should avoid guessing. options: streaming ACKs from upstream, client-supplied replay tokens, or gate side-effects at the edge.

 ben: quick take: opt-in replay with a client header. add X-RW-Replay-Key that clients provide; upstreams dedupe based on key. gateway can switch upstreams but forwards same key.

 alex: agreed. also need a way for upstream to indicate progress so gateway can resume from a checkpoint instead of full replay. propose a small response header that marks committed byte offset.

 maria: sketch of headers and semantics:

 ```
 Request:
   X-RW-Replay-Key: <uuid>      # optional; client promises idempotency semantics
 Response (upstream):
   X-RW-Stream-Commit: offset=12345   # committed byte offset the upstream will not re-execute
 ```

 alex: proposed gateway behavior:
 - if X-RW-Replay-Key present, gateway will forward the key to upstreams and may replay the request body to alternate upstreams on transient failures; upstreams must dedupe using the key
 - if X-RW-Stream-Commit returned, gateway treats bytes <= offset as acknowledged and, when switching upstreams, resumes streaming at offset (if client supports resume)
 - otherwise, gateway fast-fails to client instead of blind replay

 ben: questions: how long do replay keys live? what about resource amplification (replaying large bodies)?

 maria: TTL = configurable per-route, default 1h for high-throughput endpoints, 24h for long-running jobs. to mitigate cost, enforce per-route quotas and size limits on replayable bodies.

 taylor: browser compatibility? resuming mid-request needs custom protocol; most browsers and clients won't support resume semantics. we should limit resume to server-to-server SDKs and document fallback behavior.

 alex: yes — resume is opt-in and only in SDKs that implement chunk resumption. public browser flows get fast-fail unless they supply a replay key and are willing to accept possible replay.

 infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolling out proxy v0.42 that passthroughs X-RW-Replay-Key and X-RW-Stream-Commit to upstreams. :robot_face:

 ben: next steps: pick canonical header names, write an RFC with sequence diagrams, add unit/integration tests simulating mid-stream failover and dedupe, and sketch migration plan for SDKs. I'll open the RFC PR today.

 maria: add an example dedupe pattern for upstreams (e.g., Redis SETNX with expiry + idempotent operation guard).

 alex: good — also add observability: metrics we need: replay_attempts, replay_success, replay_tombstones, resume_fallbacks. and traces should tag replay-key so we can correlate.

 taylor: one more safety: gateway route-config should have resume_enabled boolean. default false. lint rejects resume headers on routes without opt-in.

 ben: ok filing PRs for gateway lint + route flag + RFC. :+1:

 maria: LGTM

 alex: thanks all. I'll follow up in the RFC thread with a short checklist for rollout and monitoring. :wave:
